text:
maya: FYI starting onboarding for 'aurora-7b' weights. quick checklist: weights location, tokenizer quirks, safetensors+shard naming, fp16 vs bf16 decision, TP layout. pinging folks who touched similar flows.

jin: thanks — can you drop the S3 path and the desired TP size? also any special tokenizers?

maya: s3://redwood-models/inbound/aurora-7b/v1/raw_weights.tar.gz
maya: target: serve on Dedicated (tp=4) for now, keep a fp16 export, but we should produce bf16 artifact too for private customers.

oliver: quick note about the tokenizer — source repo has tokenizer.json using byte-level BPE but missing add_prefix_space flag. that breaks starting space handling for prompts. saw this with nova models.

emily: re: shard naming — please follow our convention: aurora-7b-00001-of-00004.safetensors etc. CI expects zero-padded index. also include a manifest.txt with checksums.

maya: cheers. putting a conversion command here for review:```bash
./scripts/convert_model.py \
  --input s3://redwood-models/inbound/aurora-7b/v1/raw_weights.tar.gz \
  --out-dir /tmp/aurora-7b-safetensors \
  --dtype fp16 \
  --tp 4 \
  --shard-format "aurora-7b-{i+1:05d}-of-{n:05d}.safetensors" \
  --safetensors
```

jin: minor nit: our tools expect "-of-00004" style without dashes in the count part? earlier we normalized to `of-{n:05d}` but the suffix had to match CI regex. recommend: `aurora-7b-{i+1:05d}-of-00004.safetensors` after conversion move/rename step. also ensure the converter writes metadata header with 'model_name' and 'tp_group' if possible.

tomas: tokenizer patch: set "add_prefix_space": true, and verify unk/pad/eos ids match our serving config. sometimes pad id is 1 instead of 0 which breaks batching. run this small script to validate:```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
meta = t.get_vocab()  # quick sanity
print('has_pad', t.token_to_id('[PAD]'))
```

emily: for validation, run:```bash
sha256sum aurora-7b-*.safetensors > manifest.sha256
python tools/validate_shard_layout.py --manifest manifest.sha256 --tp 4 --expected-count 4
```

ci-bot: build-check triggered for /tmp/aurora-7b-safetensors -> job 8742 queued :gear:

maya: thanks. question: bf16 build — do we keep separate shards or a single multi-dtype archive? ops prefers separate artifacts to avoid accidental deploy.

oliver: separate artifacts please. name with dtype suffix: aurora-7b-00001-of-00004.fp16.safetensors and aurora-7b-00001-of-00004.bf16.safetensors. also include a lightweight config.json per artifact with fields: 
```
{
  "model_name": "aurora-7b",
  "tp_size": "4",
  "dtype": "fp16",
  "vocab_size": "50288"
}
```
(to be replaced with actual numbers)

maya: noted. pinging @jin for a quick CR on the conversion script and @emily for CI manifest expectations.

jin: I'll review in ~30m. if CI fails, leave artifacts in /tmp and don't overwrite s3.

emily: CI note: validator will also check tensor order (embedding first, then transformer blocks). if order mismatch we auto-fail. include a mapping file if any tensors are renamed during conversion.

maya: action items: 1) maya run conversion -> produce fp16/bf16 shards w/ correct naming 2) emily verify manifest and run validate_shard_layout.py 3) jin CR conversion script and confirm metadata headers 4) tomas patch tokenizer and confirm pad/eos ids. will update this thread when done.

oliver: small reminder — if the raw archive contains safetensors already, prefer direct shuffle+rename instead of load+save to avoid precision drift.

maya: got it. starting now, will post results (and sha256) when done. :rocket:
